in: Seeded procedural continent generator (elevation, moisture, biomes, rivers)
Terrain detail sprites (trees, reeds, rocks, dead trees, snow)
Weather: rain, storm, snow, fog, wind
Free-orbit orthographic camera, tile hover/select with info panel

stack.external_assets: none - all textures drawn procedurally to canvas at startup [ASSUMED]

art_direction.inspiration: Final Fantasy Tactics (PS1) / Final Fantasy Tactics Advance (GBA) battle maps
cues: Map is a floating diorama: a finite block of land over a dark gradient void, outer edges cut away to show layered earth/rock strata
Default view is classic isometric (azimuth 45 deg, elevation ~30 deg); free orbit still allowed
Stepped columns: textured pixel-art tile tops, darker strata/rock sides, light edge highlight on top rims
Muted, painterly earthy palette (desaturated greens, ochre, umber, slate) - not saturated
Water is semi-transparent: shallow tiles show the river bed, deep tiles darken
FFT-style cursor: flashing tile outline + floating pointer above the tile; info panel shows terrain name and height (e.g. 'Plains  h3')

rendering.upscale: largest integer scale that fits the window; letterbox remainder

camera.control: free orbit around map centre target
camera.note: Free orbit means pixels re-sample as the view turns; accepted trade-off of the free-orbit choice

rendering.lighting: one directional sun + hemisphere ambient; parameters driven by time-of-day and weather

world.units: 1 world unit = 1 tile width; 1 height step = 0.5 units

Tile.seedRand: float 0..1 (per-tile variation: texture variant, decor placement)

TerrainDef.name: display string
TerrainDef.moveCost: int (99 = impassable) - data only this phase
TerrainDef.defense: int percent - data only this phase
TerrainDef.palette: array of hex colours used by the procedural texture painter

steps: elevation = fractal noise * continent falloff, quantised to 0..8
moisture = independent fractal noise + proximity-to-water bonus

rivers = 1-2 springs on high ground (heights 3-6) following a priority-flood drainage to a lake, the sea or a front edge; each river tile one step below every bank and no higher than upstream; all shallow (wadeable)
waterfall wherever a river drops a level, and where a river leaves the board
cover: trees in clumps on woods, rocks on hills/scree/mountain/badlands, snags in swamp/bog; <= 12.5% of land, front rows thinned, clear of water, bridges and river banks; walkable, adds defense
bridges: 1 per river (2 on rivers >= 16 tiles), >= 5 apart, on straight level stretches; bridge_wood at heights 0-1, bridge_stone higher; walked at height + 1 with move cost 1

settlements by seed (village 45%, castle 30%, ruins 25%; +ruins on half the others) on the flattest dry footprint, levelled; roads = Dijkstra from the main settlement to the second and to the two cheapest board edges, gentle slopes, crossing rivers straight over a bridge (reused or new); rooftops, ramparts and ruined walls walkable
generator.controls: the HUD map picker switches to any theme or Wild Lands (reloads with ?map=<id>); R or the New map button = new random seed (written to the URL); seed shown in HUD; ?seed=N URL param; E or Save downloads the map JSON (S is taken by WASD panning); Load button or dropping a file opens a saved map, validated by parseMap

weather.wind: strength multiplier (1 = breeze; storm 3): rain slant, plant/banner sway
weather.ground: wet darkens land and cliffs; snow settles on upward tops per ground pixel, never on liquid (alpha mask), and buries flowers
weather.choice: HUD weather picker (auto = map's own: weatherForMap(seed) on Wild Lands, clear on themes), kept in the URL as weather=<kind>
weather.loop: every weather effect loops in 4 s

time_of_day.range: 0..24h; picker: the map's own light | dawn 6.5 | day 12.5 | dusk 18.4 | night 23.5 | cycle (24 h in 120 s), kept in the URL as time=<choice>
time_of_day.sun: rises right of the opening view, sets left, 62 deg at noon leaning left; moon at 40 deg by night
time_of_day.shadows: BasicShadowMap 2048, terrain/buildings/bridges cast, everything receives; subtle: sun blocked 85%, sky light 32%, scaled by time and weather
time_of_day.night: cottage windows glow, fireflies (not in rain/snow/fog), stars on clear nights; chimney smoke day and night; cloud shadows on bright days

ui.tile_info_panel: HTML overlay with pixel font: terrain (or bridge) name, height, cover standing there, move cost, defense (terrain + cover)
ui.hud: seed, weather, time, fps (debug toggle F3)

error_behavior.webgl_unavailable: show static HTML message, no crash
error_behavior.bad_seed_param: fall back to random seed and show it
error_behavior.generator_invariant_failure: throw in dev; tests guard invariants

phase2.approved_answers: 2026-10-27: all question-matrix defaults accepted; battle scenes must not be pixelated (clear, like Yggdra Union's battle scenes)

in: Pure-TS rules core: units, classes, stats, weapon triangle, terrain defence, shared MOV pool, Unions, clash maths, Morale
Pixel units on every map (matching the map props), select/move/path preview
Side-view battle scene at full screen resolution, not pixelated
Cards and turn flow, Unions, card skills, enemy AI, win/lose
out: Original Yggdra Union names, art or music

rules.stats: morale (HP, max 100-200 by class), atk, tec, gen, luk; integers 1-20 except morale

classes.axe: weapon axe; high atk, low tec
classes.bow: weapon bow; cannot counter, and a unit it attacks cannot counter
classes.mage: weapon staff; high tec, low gen
classes.knight: weapon lance; large: 1 head + 3 large soldiers; high gen

rules.weapon_triangle: sword > axe > spear(lance) > sword: +2 edge to the winner of the pair; bow and staff are outside the triangle [ASSUMED]
rules.gender: every head has one; Union shape: female leader = + (4 orthogonal neighbours), male leader = x (4 diagonal neighbours); max 5 units

movement.pool: one MOV pool per turn shared by all of a side's units (B1: fixed 12 [ASSUMED]; from B4: the card's MOV)
movement.cost: tileStats(tile).moveCost per tile entered; IMPASSABLE and blocking props cannot be entered; no height limit and no climb cost (the maps guarantee reachability on that basis)
movement.occupancy: a unit cannot end on or pass through an enemy; it may pass through allies but not end on them
movement.once: each unit moves at most once per turn

rules.terrain_defence: the defender's tileStats().defense percent reduces the Morale damage it takes

clash.edge: integer effectiveness = weapon triangle (+2/-2) + stance (aggressive +2, passive -2) + card/skill modifiers; shown as an icon
phases: charge: attacker tec vs defender gen + edge -> defender soldiers lost; a luk crit can down the head (panic: defender loses its counter)
counter: defender tec vs attacker gen -> attacker soldiers lost; skipped for bows and when attacked by a bow
melee: one-on-one duels, win chance from atk vs atk + edge, until one side has no fighters; luk gives flash attacks
clash.result: loser loses Morale = card POW x (0.5 + 0.08 per winning small soldier left, 0.16 per large) + 10 if winner head alive, minus loser terrain defence %; winner loses nothing [ASSUMED: formula shape after Yggdra Union, numbers tuned in play]
clash.rng: seeded per battle, so every battle replays exactly in tests
clash.morale_zero: the unit is defeated and leaves the map
clash.engine: a step-by-step simulation (ClashSim) the battle scene drives one event at a time, so the stance can change mid-battle; resolveClash runs it to the end with fixed stances

rules.cards: POW, MOV, ACE (weapon needed to fire the skill, or All), skill; a hand of 8 per battle [ASSUMED]; each card used once per battle; one card per turn
rules.turn: pick card -> move units (shared pool) -> at most one attack -> end turn -> enemy turn
rules.win_lose: win: every enemy defeated; lose: every player unit defeated [ASSUMED: no leader-death rule yet]

map_units.art: procedural pixel art drawn in code like the props, rendered through the map's pixel pipeline; about one tile tall (~28 px)
map_units.animation: idle loop, walk, hop on height steps; facing follows movement
map_units.deployment: auto-placed on walkable, reachable, prop-free tiles: player near the front edge (nearest the opening camera), enemy near the back
map_units.interaction: mouse click or arrows + Z select; move range highlight; path preview on hover; Z/click confirm; X cancel; Enter end turn; camera eases to the selected unit; unit panel shows name, class, Morale, stats, tile defence
map_units.viewer_mode: the map viewer (no units) stays available from the menu

battle_scene.look: side-on, two squads facing each other across a wide horizon, HUD on top; reference: Yggdra Union's battle scenes
battle_scene.resolution: drawn at the canvas's full device resolution (CSS size x devicePixelRatio), antialiased; NOT through the 480x270 pixel pipeline; textures smooth (linear filtering, mipmaps)
battle_scene.art: raster art generated by the user in Google Flow from prompts I write (approved 2026-10-27), on a flat #00FF00 background; I key out the green, remove spill, crop, align and pack it into per-class atlases loaded only for the classes in the current battle; drawn at full resolution with linear filtering and mipmaps
battle_scene.clips: idle, run, attack, hit, fall, cheer; heads have a distinct look per class and side
battle_scene.backdrop: painted at full resolution with smooth paths in the theme's colours: sky, two parallax silhouette layers chosen by the theme's category, ground from the two fighters' tile palettes (each side stands on its own tile's ground)
battle_scene.hud: both heads' names and Morale bars, soldiers left, edge icon, stance (from B3), skill gauge (from B3); HTML/CSS overlay at full resolution with a clear font
battle_scene.transition: map -> battle -> map, back on the same camera view
battle_scene.risk: if Flow art fails the style frame, fall back to code-painted cut-out characters or a licensed art pack
battle_scene.animation: decided by the round 2 test on one class: pose images (4-6 crisp key poses per clip) vs Flow video clips (Frames to Video, same first and last frame for loops) cut into frames; either way the battle plays sprite clips driven by the rules, never a video
battle_scene.roster: 18 designs: 6 leaders per side (one per class, about 3 female and 3 male each) + 6 soldier designs shared by both sides, recoloured red in code for the enemy (24 if the recolour does not hold up); later 12 leader portraits, backgrounds per theme or category, card art

leader_looks.player: heroes: each has a signature colour of their own (not just team blue), a silhouette readable at a distance (distinctive hair, cape, scarf or plume, ornate trim) and a signature weapon; a blue team accent (sash or plume) plus the blue banner and HUD mark the side
leader_looks.enemy: a rival army with one shared look: darker, heavier armour, closed helms or crowns, crimson and black, sharper angular shapes; each still a unique design
leader_looks.soldiers: only soldiers are shared and recoloured red for the enemy; leaders are never recolours
leader_looks.in_game: player leaders get a portrait in the battle banner, later a subtle glow or pennant on the map
leader_looks.timing: leader art is generated after the round 2 animation test decides how many images each leader needs

rounds: round 1: one sword leader, one sword soldier, one meadow background -> still style frame in the engine for approval
round 2: animation test on the sword class, pose images vs video, side by side in the engine
then: the rest of the roster, portraits, backgrounds, card art
battle_scene.naming: prompts never name Yggdra Union or its artists; README credits Google Flow

milestones: B2 battle scene v0 (style frame first, then scripted animation)

file_layout.src/game/: pure rules core, no three.js (units, movement, union, clash, cards, turn, ai)
file_layout.src/battle/: battle scene: renderer path, rig/parts, painter, director, backdrop
file_layout.src/ui/: unit panel, battle HUD, card hand
